local_market_context: Edmonton therapy searches are usually specific: a psychologist downtown, counselling near Whyte Avenue, trauma therapy in the west end, or an Alberta-licensed clinician who works online with people across the province. Someone may also be filtering by approach, cost, availability or experience with a particular population. A page that only offers “therapy in Edmonton” does little for that person.

We organise the site around those searches: a clear homepage, specialty pages, and an office or service-area page covering the Edmonton neighbourhoods and nearby communities the practice serves. Internal links connect the concern, the clinician and the practical steps to book.

We then fix the foundations that let those pages perform: crawlable navigation, descriptive titles and headings, quick mobile layouts and metadata that reflects the content. Edmonton and Alberta are named where they are accurate, not sprinkled through the copy.

Edmonton is a capital city with a particular shape: government, health and university employment, a dense core around Oliver and downtown, student streets around Garneau and the University of Alberta, and older commercial strips like Old Strathcona along Whyte Avenue. Practices here also draw from St. Albert, Sherwood Park and Spruce Grove, so a site that only names Edmonton can miss the surrounding capital region. Where a clinician genuinely sees clients from those communities, saying so is more useful than another identical page.

Registration through the College of Alberta Psychologists, and the province's rules for telehealth and advertising, shape how a page can be written: which titles a clinician may use, what a practice may claim and how a first appointment is described. We treat those as constraints rather than marketing opportunities, and keep the wording about services, fees and availability in line with what the practice actually offers.

Edmonton searches also follow the river valley and the ring roads. Someone in Mill Woods is a long drive from Callingwood, and a page that claims to serve "all of Edmonton" without naming a part of town reads as generic to a client who knows the city. Group practices with clinicians in different quadrants are usually better served by one page per real office, plus a service-area statement that matches where sessions actually happen.

ai.heading: What an AI search optimization agency does for Edmonton therapists
paragraphs: When someone asks an AI assistant for a trauma therapist in Edmonton, a counsellor near Whyte Avenue or an online psychologist licensed in Alberta, the response is built from sources the tool can read and trust. Clear, consistent pages give it the facts: who the clinician helps, where they are registered, what they specialise in and how to arrange a first appointment.

AI search optimization, or AI SEO, is the work of getting a practice understood and cited by those tools. Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the related practice of writing pages that provide direct, extractable answers. Generative engine optimization (GEO) is about keeping the practice described accurately across the sources AI systems consult. Our AI search optimization services explain the wider programme.

The labels overlap, and each describes part of the same SEO work rather than a separate magic service. No agency can guarantee a citation or a placement in AI answers. As an AI search optimization agency, what we can do is make the facts about your Edmonton practice easy to find, quote and repeat.

faq_heading: AI search optimization and GEO questions from Edmonton therapists

faqs.q: Can a solo practice rank for “psychologist Edmonton”?
faqs.a: A solo practice can compete for Edmonton searches when the site is clear about its work and the communities it serves. Google rewards focused specialty pages, a complete Google Business Profile, genuine reviews and a fast mobile site. We target realistic searches rather than promising a position.

faqs.q: Is SEO useful if all sessions are online?
faqs.a: Yes. People still search for an Alberta-registered therapist, a specific specialty or a clinician who offers telehealth from Edmonton. The site should state that sessions are online, which parts of Alberta you serve and how the first appointment works.

faqs.q: Should the site mention St. Albert, Sherwood Park or Mill Woods?
faqs.a: Name the places the practice genuinely serves on the office or service-area page. A clear service-area section is more useful than a thin duplicate page for every quadrant or nearby city. If a community produces real demand, it may deserve its own page later, but not one that repeats the same copy.

No specific timeline is promised. Google sets the pace, and rankings depend on the starting site, the competition, the review profile and how consistently the work is maintained. The first visible progress is the work itself — fixes, new pages and rewritten titles — followed by reports on which searches the pages appear for.

The engagement is a 3-month implementation project with three packages — Starter ($329.99/month), Professional ($379.99/month) and Premium ($429.99/month) — paid over 12 monthly installments. The monthly amount is a payment toward the project, not an ongoing retainer. A group practice with several clinicians may need a larger scope, confirmed in writing after a free review.

faqs.q: Do you work with group practices?
faqs.a: Yes. A group practice often needs a clearer structure: who each clinician is, which specialties and populations they serve, where sessions happen and how inquiries are routed. We can plan the site around the group as a whole without losing the individual clinicians a client may be looking for.

faqs.q: Does your marketing respect Alberta licensing bodies and professional ethics rules?
faqs.a: We avoid guarantees, clinical claims and misleading wording. Marketing should describe the practice accurately, not promise a ranking or an outcome. The practice remains responsible for its own compliance with Alberta regulatory bodies and professional obligations, and we flag anything that may need a closer review.
